verdicts.facing: none (terrain, one top-down surface per subject.json)
verdicts.why: The brief does not decide tiling seams on a terrain. No lettered line covers a terrain that does not tile cleanly, and B1a (no outlines) is about a sprite's silhouette, which a terrain does not have, so I do not stretch it into a REDO. The defect is real and I measured it. The texture has a 1‑px dark border on all four edges: row 0 has mean luminance 76.5 and row 1023 has 75.8; column 0 has 77.1 and column 1023 has 74.1. The interior is about 82. Just inside the dark edge is a brighter ring (row 1 at 84.7, column 1 at 84.8), which looks like a sharpening halo. In tiled_2x2.png, two dark edges meet at each join, so every repeat shows a thin dark grid line. It is visible in the full 2x2 view and plain at 3x zoom on the centre join. Every other line passes. The picture is our own: it is red sand with grey-green pollution blotches, and its fine detail is uncorrelated with the grey-brown donor_standin.png (r=0.0004) and with sibling_unpolluted.png (r=0.007). It is fully opaque with no alpha artefacts. No owner keep or note applies (subject.json).
verdicts.seen: a dark 1-px border ringed by a 1-px bright halo on all four edges of terrain.png, which makes a visible grid line at every join in tiled_2x2.png
verdicts.notes: Fix if the window wants one: crop or re-wrap the edges (for example, offset by half the canvas and heal the old edges, or copy each edge row and column from the row or column next to it) so the wrap difference matches the interior. This is a rerun, not a redraw. A concern that blocks nothing: the candidate is much softer than its unpolluted sibling (high-frequency std 2.9 against 11.2; luminance std 4.0 against 11.2), so the fine sand grain mostly gives way to soft blotches. The sibling is not an owner keep, so B3 does not bind.

proposals: Add a terrain tiling line (proposed G1 or D5): a terrain texture must wrap edge to edge with no seam visible in a 2x2 tiling. The test: luminance and colour across the wrap boundary (row 0 against row N-1, column 0 against column N-1) should differ by no more than the difference between neighbouring interior rows, and the edge rows should have no dark or bright border. Evidence: terrain.png has dark edge rows and columns (about 76 against an interior of about 82) with a bright halo one pixel in, and this shows as a grid in tiled_2x2.png. Today no lettered line can refuse it.

Say how B3 applies to a polluted terrain variant: should it match its unpolluted sibling's grain and scale even when the sibling is not an owner keep? terrain.png is markedly softer and lower in contrast than sibling_unpolluted.png, and the brief does not say whether that matters.
